newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Red Cross appeals for $6 mln for Iran quake aid.
newsitem.headline: Red Cross appeals for $6 mln for Iran quake aid.

text.p: The world Red Cross body appealed on Wednesday for cash to help 60,000 people left homeless by a powerful earthquake in Iran that killed up to 1,000 people.

The Geneva-based International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies said in a statement it needed nine million Swiss Francs ($6.1 million) to help the Iranian Red Crescent's emergency relief work.

The quake on Friday, measuring 5.5 on the Richter scale, completely destroyed 20 villages and damaged 80 others in the mountainous northwest. It was followed by 500 aftershocks and another quake measuring 5.2 on Sunday.
Aid started to trickle in after Iran's first appeal for foreign help in at least 10 years. Switzerland, Britain, Japan and some international agencies have offered aid.
A powerful quake killed 35,000 people in Iran in 1990. In February, two quakes measuring 6.1 and 5.4 on the Richter scale killed at least 79 people and injured 260 in the northeast.
